rail: OPK terminal known EVM network profiles
notes: Every enabled network is pinned in the native apps; provisioning QR payloads cannot supply or override these trust anchors.

Base Mainnet is listed first for stable presentation and is the production application default; Base Sepolia remains available for explicit testing. Reusable SDK callers still select a network explicitly.
The CREATE2 example vault is a deterministic test input, not a deployed merchant vault.
Each vault runtime code hash is the exact deployed OPK Protocol 1.6 proxy runtime for that network; it intentionally does not use a zero-immutable browser-deployer artifact hash.
The CREATE2 vectors use the same example vault and invoice ID so implementations can prove that network-specific factory and receiver implementation constants produce the published receiver.
One payment profile selects exactly one network, vault, and payment asset for an invoice.
The Base Mainnet and Base Sepolia pins were verified against OPK Protocol commit 4629fb3fe5cd0d4d23676fe6b80b89fb097b7512 and its Route A records under contracts/deployments.
The public Base RPC endpoints are rate-limited and are not suitable production-provider guarantees; operators should review endpoint capacity before handling live volume.
A vault on this pinned stack offers the native asset only after NATIVE_ASSET() succeeds with the EIP-7528 sentinel and isPaymentToken(sentinel) is true.

The compiled confirmation value is a floor and fresh-network default. A merchant administrator may choose a network policy at or above the floor; every profile on that chain shares it, and the provisioning QR cannot override it.
